concurrencyRaceResults.description: two concurrent workers race to reserve a single-use bounded authority
three concurrent identical reservation attempts for the same intent
two workers persist the identical execution receipt concurrently
two workers persist contradictory receipts for one reservation concurrently
two workers durably bind conflicting authorization lineage to the same P6 consequence

transitionLedgerTamperResults.method: raw SQL INSERT jumping to a future sequence_no, bypassing the reservation-table trigger
raw SQL INSERT with event_digest not matching PostgreSQL's own digest() recomputation over the payload

mutationTestResults.note: unreachable via normal API since putObject() enforces the same invariant at write time; added a direct-SQL-bypass test to exercise the defense-in-depth path
required mutating the migration file itself; the test's own migration helper re-applies migration 008 (including CREATE TRIGGER) before every run, which silently undid an out-of-band DROP TRIGGER

mutationTestResultsCaveat: Time-boxed to the highest-value protections explicitly named in the mission (expiry, revocation, tenant isolation, append-only ledger). Receipt-uniqueness and authorization-binding-conflict enforcement were verified via passing concurrency/conflict tests (see concurrencyRaceResults) rather than live constraint-drop mutation, because the receipt-bindings table has FK-dependent tables and a risky cascading DROP CONSTRAINT was judged not worth the blast radius on a shared disposable database for this pass.

cedar.installMethod: npm install --save (real package manager, package-lock.json updated)
defectsFoundAndFixed: checkParsePolicySet/validate/isAuthorized require policies as a PolicySet struct ({ staticPolicies: text }), not a raw string — adapter was passing a raw string
this cedar-wasm version returns lowercase decision values ("allow"/"deny"), not "Allow"/"Deny" — adapter compared against the wrong case, which would have silently DENIED every real ALLOW decision

ciFixed.defect: omnia-v9-closure job's last step ran 'node --test tests/omnia-v9-closure.test.mjs', which does not exist in the repository; reproduced locally as exit code 1
ciFixed.fix: pointed the step at the real file, tests/omnia-v9-end-to-end-proof-circuit.test.mjs

implementationDefectsFixed.description: parseTime()/finiteTime() compared node-postgres Date objects via Date.parse(String(value)), which invokes Date.prototype.toString() and truncates to whole-second precision. Caused spurious P9 chain-verification failures against real PostgreSQL, and in the P8 reconciler could let a reservation created up to ~1s after a pre-effect observation appear to have existed before it.
implementationDefectsFixed.howFound: running the existing 'real PostgreSQL atomically captures direct authority mutations...' test against a genuine local PostgreSQL 16 instance instead of PGlite
